tagline: Six miles of causeway over a lake that would not drain.
intro: NC 94 leaves US 264 at New Holland and heads north onto a causeway nearly six miles long across Lake Mattamuskeet, the largest natural lake in North Carolina and only a few feet deep. Beyond the lake the road goes in and out of swamp and low farmland to Columbia on the Scuppernong River, then turns east on US 64 through Alligator, past the refuge, to Manns Harbor and across the sound to Roanoke Island.

Some of the farmland here was once swamp, drained by canals in a practice called swamp busting that is no longer allowed. The Alligator River refuge to the east was set aside in 1984 for the pocosin, a wetland of its own kind.

moments.title: Lake Mattamuskeet
moments.text: Between 1911 and 1934 investors tried to pump this 50,000-acre lake dry for farms, then the last owner sold it to the government for a migratory bird refuge.

moments.title: Columbia
moments.text: Near the Tyrrell County seat lies Somerset Place, a plantation dating from 1785 that was home to more than 300 enslaved men, women and children.

moments.title: Manns Harbor
moments.text: A fishing village named for a German captain who sheltered here from a storm, where a ferry crossed to Roanoke Island until the bridge was finished in 1957.
